ui.name: Maine Department of Labor, Unemployment Insurance Tax

epay.text: Taxpayers with a combined annual tax liability for all taxes that is $10,000 or more for the prior calendar year must remit all Maine tax payments electronically and continue to remit tax payments electronically in future years. Thus employers and non-wage payers required to remit on a semiweekly basis must do so electronically.

returns.name: Form 941ME, Quarterly Return of Income Tax Withholding
contents: Filed by every employer or non-payroll filer registered to remit withholding, even when no tax was withheld; the withholding detail pages must be completed (a waiver is needed otherwise).
Reports the quarter's withholding, reconciles payments, and pays any balance due.
Semiweekly payments are made with Form 900ME (electronically for semiweekly payers).

deposits.interpretation: Maine's withholding system works like the federal one. An employer or non-wage payer whose total withholding in the look-back period (July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2025 for 2026) was $18,000 or MORE pays SEMIWEEKLY: wages paid Wednesday, Thursday or Friday are due the following Wednesday, wages paid Saturday to Tuesday the following Friday. All others pay on or before the quarterly return due date: Form 941ME, due the last day of the month following the end of the quarter, even if there is no tax to report. The account is reviewed at the end of 2026 for 2027, and the State Tax Assessor may require more frequent remittances if collection is in jeopardy (not modelled). The quarterly return reports and reconciles the quarter's payments and pays any balance.

lookback.description: Maine withholding in the look-back period July 1 to June 30 before the calendar year

channels.description: Maine Tax Portal (MTP) at revenue.maine.gov; the booklet carries a section on payroll processors, including that processors must be licensed with the Bureau of Consumer Credit Protection and have posted surety or be enrolled in the Payroll Processor Recovery Fund
enrollment: Register for Maine withholding through the Maine Tax Portal (accounts are closed there or with Form 941BN-ME).

A payroll processor handling client funds in Maine should be licensed with the Bureau of Consumer Credit Protection (207-624-8527) with proof of fidelity insurance, and have a surety bond or letter of credit or be enrolled in the state's Payroll Processor Recovery Fund; the booklet advises clients to require this, and that notices from tax agencies go to the client.

returns.name: Unemployment Contributions Quarterly Report (Form ME UC-1)
contents: Due by or on the last day of the month after the end of each calendar quarter (April 30, July 31, October 31, January 31).
The form calculates the quarter's unemployment contributions and reports employee wages.
